gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured power output for a car head unit. BestCarAudio bench-tested a source unit at about 1% THD+N into 4 Ω and got 12.81 W at 12.0 V, 18.75 W at 14.4 V and 20.2 W at 15 V. That is far below the '50 W × 4' figure that Abt prints for the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT ChatGPT recommends.
standout_why: I read Abt (result 6) and Sonic Electronix (result 14) from ChatGPT's results. Abt shows only 'MOSFET 50W x 4' with no basis. Sonic Electronix already separates '22 watts x 4' RMS from '50 watts x 4' peak, so part of the point is covered. Neither page, and none of the others in ChatGPT's results that I could check, carries a lab measurement. I could not open the cited Crutchfield guide, which returned HTTP 403, so I can't rule out that it covers the RMS-vs-peak point. World Wide Stereo's guide (Chris Mulhearn, updated 2026-08-28) has no measurements. I found no named lab measurement for any of the candidate models. The only measurement I found is a general bench test of a head unit whose maker and model BestCarAudio doesn't name.
decides: It doesn't decide between the candidates, because no named reviewer or lab has measured any of them. It confirms one way to compare them: use the continuous (CTA-2006/RMS) rating, about 20 to 22 W per channel, and ignore the 50 to 55 W 'max' figures. Bench tests show a built-in head-unit amp gives about 13 to 20 W into 4 Ω, depending on supply voltage. A shopper who wants more volume should budget for an external amp, and the preamp output voltage (4 V on the Pioneer per Abt and Sonic Electronix, 2 V on the Sony per BestCarAudio) matters more than the headline wattage.

unsourced: A named lab or reviewer measurement (output power, preamp voltage, S/N, frequency response, Bluetooth codec bandwidth) for the Pioneer DEH-S4220BT, JVC KD-T920BTS, Sony MEX-N5300BT, Kenwood KDC-BT282U/BT370U or Pioneer FH-S722BS. I searched BestCarAudio, Audio Science Review (its car audio section and SINAD database), German labs (Car&Hifi, autohifi, testbericht.de, hifi-forum.de) and general bench/oscilloscope tests. I found only maker ratings, user reviews and autoradio-test.org's unmeasured 8.10 score for the Sony.
